newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African ex-security chief stalls truth body.
newsitem.headline: S.African ex-security chief stalls truth body.

text.p: The former head of a secret South African military unit refused on Tuesday to answer questions from the country's truth commission on his foreign agents or operations, the commission said.

It said in a statement that Joe Verster, former managing director of the Civil Cooperation Bureau (CCB), also balked at having his picture taken by press photographers on the grounds that it would put his life in danger.
But the commission ordered that photographers be allowed access to him during a closed-door interrogation by commission investigators "in the interests of openness and transparency".
"I was not convinced that his life or career would be at risk if his photograph appeared in the media," commission chief investigator Dumisa Ntsebeza said.
"The commission has a witness protection programme but he refused to apply for that.
"In the case of foreign operations and operatives who worked under him, I gave an undertaking that the inquiry could not be used by foreign attorneys-general to prosecute him or anybody he names."

But Ntsebeza said Verster continued to refuse to answer questions on foreign operations of the CCB, set up by the previous apartheid government to counter the African National Congress and other banned black liberation groups.

Ntsebeza said he warned Verster he could be fined or jailed if he refused to cooperate with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up in 1995 to uncover as much as possible of human rights crimes during apartheid.
